concepts/wiki-compilation.title: Wiki Compilation
concepts/wiki-compilation.summary: The LLM-driven pipeline that converts raw ingested documents into a structured, cross-linked markdown wiki with source summaries and concept articles.

concepts/wikipedia-knowledge-model.title: Wikipedia Knowledge Model
concepts/wikipedia-knowledge-model.summary: Wikipedia's collaborative editorial model — anyone can edit, consensus-driven quality improvement, verifiability over truth, no original research — represents the most successful collective knowledge creation system in history, now under unprecedented stress from AI.

concepts/wisdom-of-crowds.title: Wisdom of Crowds
concepts/wisdom-of-crowds.summary: Aggregated independent judgments from diverse groups outperform individual experts — mathematically formalized by Page's Diversity Prediction Theorem — but requiring conditions (diversity, independence, decentralization, aggregation) that AI both enables and threatens.

concepts/wordpiece.title: WordPiece
concepts/wordpiece.summary: BERT-family tokenization algorithm similar to BPE but merging token pairs that maximize training data likelihood rather than simple frequency — producing more linguistically informative merges.

concepts/world-models.title: World Models
concepts/world-models.summary: AI systems that build internal representations of reality to simulate, predict, and plan — the emerging paradigm challenging LLMs as the path to general intelligence, with $1.3B+ in 2026 funding across AMI Labs, DeepMind, NVIDIA, and World Labs.

concepts/yaml-frontmatter.title: YAML Frontmatter
concepts/yaml-frontmatter.summary: YAML frontmatter is the de facto standard for embedding structured metadata in markdown files — enabling queryability, categorization, and machine processing while preserving plain-text readability.

concepts/zero-optimizer.title: ZeRO Optimizer
concepts/zero-optimizer.summary: DeepSpeed's Zero Redundancy Optimizer progressively shards optimizer states (Stage 1), gradients (Stage 2), and parameters (Stage 3) across data-parallel GPUs, reducing per-GPU memory by up to the parallelism degree while preserving data parallelism's simplicity.

concepts/zero-shot-information-extractio.title: Zero-Shot Information Extraction
concepts/zero-shot-information-extractio.summary: Extracting entities, relations, and structured data from text without any task-specific training examples — enabled by LLMs' general language understanding and instruction-following abilities.

concepts/zero-shot-prompting.title: Zero-Shot Prompting
concepts/zero-shot-prompting.summary: Direct instruction to an LLM without any demonstration examples — the simplest prompting approach, and the recommended starting point before reaching for more complex techniques.

concepts/zettelkasten.title: Zettelkasten
concepts/zettelkasten.summary: Niklas Luhmann's slip-box method for personal knowledge management: atomic, hypertextually linked notes that form a 'communication partner' for thinking — the foundational methodology behind modern networked note-taking tools.

entities/addy-osmani.title: Addy Osmani
entities/addy-osmani.summary: Google Chrome engineering lead who published an influential 10-step LLM coding workflow for 2026 — advocating spec-first planning, model rotation, and the human as 'director of the show.'

entities/agentic-ai-foundation.title: Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
entities/agentic-ai-foundation.summary: Linux Foundation directed fund governing MCP, co-founded by Anthropic, Block, and OpenAI in December 2025. Supported by Google, Microsoft, AWS, Cloudflare, Bloomberg. Mission: ensure agentic AI evolves transparently and in the public interest.

entities/aider.title: Aider
entities/aider.summary: Open-source CLI-based AI coding agent with Git-native workflow, transparent diffs, and model flexibility — the leading open-source alternative to proprietary coding agents.

entities/alphafold.title: AlphaFold
entities/alphafold.summary: DeepMind's protein structure prediction system that earned a Nobel Prize in Chemistry — predicts 3D structures of proteins with near-experimental accuracy, transforming biology and drug discovery.

entities/andrej-karpathy.title: Andrej Karpathy
entities/andrej-karpathy.summary: Slovak-Canadian AI researcher, educator, and entrepreneur: OpenAI co-founder, Tesla AI Director, creator of Software 2.0 and vibe coding, builder of micrograd/nanoGPT/llm.c, founder of Eureka Labs, and originator of the LLM knowledge base methodology that inspired this wiki.

entities/andrew-ng.title: Andrew Ng
entities/andrew-ng.summary: AI researcher and educator who popularized the four agentic AI design patterns (reflection, tool use, planning, multi-agent collaboration) and advocates architecture-over-model-size for enterprises.

entities/andy-matuschak.title: Andy Matuschak
entities/andy-matuschak.summary: Software engineer, researcher, and independent thinker who developed the evergreen notes framework — five principles for durable, evolving notes that build intellectual capital over time — and pioneered public sliding-pane note systems.

entities/anki.title: Anki
entities/anki.summary: Open-source spaced repetition software using the FSRS algorithm to schedule adaptive review of flashcards — the most sophisticated and widely used SRS platform, integrable with PKM tools like Obsidian.

entities/anthropic-hh-rlhf.title: Anthropic HH-RLHF Dataset
entities/anthropic-hh-rlhf.summary: Foundational open preference dataset with 170K human comparisons for training helpful and harmless AI assistants — collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk, using chosen/rejected pair format.

entities/anthropic.title: Anthropic
entities/anthropic.summary: AI safety PBC founded 2021 by 7 ex-OpenAI researchers (Dario & Daniela Amodei + 5); $380B valuation; builds Claude models, Claude Code ($2.5B ARR), and MCP; ranked #1 in FLI AI Safety Index.

entities/apache-airflow.title: Apache Airflow
entities/apache-airflow.summary: Dominant workflow orchestration platform (35% of enterprise AI/ML pipelines): Python-native DAG definitions, event-driven scheduling (3.0), dynamic task mapping, and integrations with SageMaker/Databricks/vector DBs.

entities/attention-is-all-you-need.title: Attention Is All You Need
entities/attention-is-all-you-need.summary: The 2017 paper by Vaswani et al. introducing the Transformer architecture — the most cited ML paper of the 21st century, replacing RNNs/CNNs with pure attention and enabling all modern LLMs.

entities/beautiful-soup.title: Beautiful Soup
entities/beautiful-soup.summary: Python's most popular HTML/XML parsing library — lightweight, handles malformed markup gracefully, often used with requests for simple scraping or with Playwright for hybrid JS+parsing workflows.

entities/bert.title: BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers)
entities/bert.summary: Google's 2018 encoder-only transformer using bidirectional Masked Language Modeling — revolutionized NLP understanding tasks but cannot generate text. 110M (base) to 340M (large) parameters.

entities/cameron-wolfe.title: Cameron R. Wolfe
entities/cameron-wolfe.summary: Ph.D. researcher and author of the 'Deep (Learning) Focus' newsletter, producing detailed technical deep-dives on DPO, reward models, RLAIF, and other LLM alignment topics.

entities/chatbot-arena.title: Chatbot Arena (Arena AI)
entities/chatbot-arena.summary: Crowdsourced LLM evaluation platform: anonymous pairwise battles with 300+ models and 1.5M+ preferences, using Elo/Bradley-Terry scoring from organic user queries — the most widely-cited dynamic benchmark.

entities/chinchilla.title: Chinchilla
entities/chinchilla.summary: DeepMind's 2022 paper establishing compute-optimal scaling laws: model parameters and training tokens should scale equally (~20 tokens per parameter), showing many existing LLMs were significantly undertrained.

entities/chromadb.title: ChromaDB
entities/chromadb.summary: An open-source embedding database used in Gallagher's Knowledge Graph Kit to provide semantic vector search over graph nodes alongside SQLite structural storage.

entities/claimify.title: Claimify
entities/claimify.summary: Microsoft Research's 4-stage claim extraction system (ACL 2025) that decomposes LLM outputs into atomic verifiable claims with 99% source entailment.

entities/claude-code.title: Claude Code
entities/claude-code.summary: Anthropic's agentic coding tool: reads codebases, edits files, runs tests, creates PRs — $2.5B annualized revenue by March 2026, leading SWE-bench Verified at 80.9%.

entities/claude.title: Claude
entities/claude.summary: Anthropic's frontier LLM family named after Claude Shannon; spans four generations (Claude 1-4.6) with Opus/Sonnet/Haiku tiers, up to 1M context, adaptive thinking, and market-leading coding benchmarks.

entities/clip.title: CLIP
entities/clip.summary: OpenAI's Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining model (2021): dual text/image encoders producing 512-dim shared embeddings via contrastive learning; foundational for multimodal search, RAG, and image generation.

entities/coderabbit.title: CodeRabbit
entities/coderabbit.summary: The most widely installed AI code review app on GitHub/GitLab — 2M+ repos, 13M+ PRs processed, free for open source — but has the highest false-positive rate among major review tools.

entities/codestral.title: Codestral
entities/codestral.summary: Mistral AI's open-weight coding model (22B parameters) -- fast local inference at 1.4s per response vs Claude's 2.1s, scoring within 85-90% of frontier models on straightforward tasks.

entities/cognee.title: Cognee
entities/cognee.summary: Cognitive memory layer for agentic AI systems. Hybrid graph + vector embeddings in unified memory. Modular extraction pipelines, multiple graph backends (NetworkX, FalkorDB, Neo4j), 30+ data source connectors, incremental learning without full reprocessing.

entities/collective-intelligence-project.title: Collective Intelligence Project (CIP)
entities/collective-intelligence-project.summary: Nonprofit R&D lab (founded by Divya Siddarth and Saffron Huang) building collective intelligence mechanisms for AI governance — including Collective Constitutional AI with Anthropic and Global Dialogues with 1,000 participants from 70+ countries.

entities/colpali.title: ColPali
entities/colpali.summary: ColBERT-like multimodal retrieval model using VLMs as image encoders: produces multiple vectors per token with MaxSim similarity for direct visual document retrieval without OCR, evaluated on ViDoRe benchmark.

entities/common-crawl.title: Common Crawl
entities/common-crawl.summary: Non-profit web crawl archive releasing monthly snapshots of petabytes of raw web data — the foundational data source for virtually all open LLM pretraining datasets.

entities/confluence.title: Confluence
entities/confluence.summary: Atlassian's structured wiki and documentation platform for enterprise knowledge management. Includes Rovo AI with 20+ pre-built documentation agents. Deep Jira integration (76% of customers ship faster). Pricing from $5.42/user/month. Best fit for technical teams in the Atlassian ecosystem.

entities/crawl4ai.title: Crawl4AI
entities/crawl4ai.summary: The #1 trending open-source web crawler (63K+ GitHub stars) — Playwright-based async crawler producing LLM-ready markdown with BM25 relevance filtering, multi-strategy extraction, and anti-bot detection.

entities/cursor.title: Cursor
entities/cursor.summary: AI-native IDE (VS Code fork) that leads the market with $2B+ ARR and $29.3B valuation by March 2026 — praised for 'magical' inline editing, codebase indexing, and agent mode.

entities/cyc-project.title: Cyc Project
entities/cyc-project.summary: AI's most ambitious knowledge engineering project (1984-present): 40 years encoding common-sense knowledge into 1.5M terms and 24.5M assertions in CycL — a cautionary tale and proof of concept for explicit knowledge representation.

entities/dairai.title: DAIR.AI
entities/dairai.summary: An AI education and research organization whose Academy published the definitive system architecture analysis of Karpathy's LLM knowledge base methodology.

entities/daniela-amodei.title: Daniela Amodei
entities/daniela-amodei.summary: President and co-founder of Anthropic; former VP of Operations at OpenAI; co-leads the company with her brother Dario Amodei.

entities/dario-amodei.title: Dario Amodei
entities/dario-amodei.summary: CEO and co-founder of Anthropic; former VP of Research at OpenAI; author of 'Machines of Loving Grace' essay articulating AI's transformative upside across biology, governance, and economics.

entities/dataview.title: Dataview
entities/dataview.summary: The most important Obsidian power-user plugin: a SQL-like query engine over vault metadata supporting DQL, inline queries, and JavaScript — with Datacore as its next-gen successor.

entities/dclm.title: DCLM (DataComp-LM)
entities/dclm.summary: Benchmark and dataset from Apple/UW for controlled training data experiments — provides 240T-token Common Crawl pool, 53 evaluations, and the DCLM-Baseline (2T tokens) achieving 64% MMLU on a 7B model.

entities/dean-allemang.title: Dean Allemang
entities/dean-allemang.summary: Knowledge graph and semantic web expert who demonstrated that LLMs natively understand OWL ontologies, arguing that ontologies and property graphs are complementary rather than competing.

entities/deepeval.title: DeepEval
entities/deepeval.summary: Open-source LLM evaluation framework by Confident AI with 14+ built-in metrics (hallucination, faithfulness, toxicity, bias), Pytest-like unit testing paradigm, and CI/CD integration.

entities/deepseek-v3.title: DeepSeek V3
entities/deepseek-v3.summary: Chinese AI lab's 671B-parameter MoE model trained for a reported $5.6M — challenging the assumption that frontier LLMs require $100M+ budgets, though the figure excluded infrastructure, experimentation, and failed runs.

entities/deepseek.title: DeepSeek
entities/deepseek.summary: Chinese AI lab whose R1 model (Jan 2025) triggered the 'DeepSeek moment' — demonstrating frontier reasoning at dramatically lower cost; V3.2 (685B, MIT) surpassed GPT-5-High on math.

entities/deepspeed.title: DeepSpeed
entities/deepspeed.summary: Microsoft's open-source deep learning optimization library, best known for the ZeRO optimizer that progressively shards optimizer states, gradients, and parameters to enable training of models that exceed single-GPU memory.

entities/deplot.title: DePlot
entities/deplot.summary: Google's specialized tool for converting charts and plots into structured text (linearized tables), used in multimodal RAG preprocessing to make visual data accessible to text-based LLMs.

entities/derek-sivers.title: Derek Sivers
entities/derek-sivers.summary: Programmer, author, and entrepreneur who has written exclusively in plain text since 1990 — the most prominent individual advocate for plain-text-as-productivity-system.

entities/devin-ai.title: Devin AI
entities/devin-ai.summary: First autonomous AI software engineer by Cognition Labs (2024): shell + editor + browser in sandbox, 13.86% SWE-bench at launch, $20/month with 2.0.

entities/devin.title: Devin
entities/devin.summary: The first 'AI software engineer' by Cognition Labs (March 2024) — operates autonomously with its own shell, browser, and editor; Devin 2.0 (April 2025) dropped price from $500/mo to $20/mo.

entities/docling.title: Docling
entities/docling.summary: IBM open-source document parsing toolkit (MIT): DocLayNet layout analysis + TableFormer table recognition, outputs AI-ready JSON/Markdown, 9/10 performance, ideal for enterprise RAG in air-gapped environments.

entities/doug-lenat.title: Doug Lenat
entities/doug-lenat.summary: American AI researcher (1950-2023) who founded the Cyc project in 1984 and spent 39 years building the world's largest hand-encoded common-sense knowledge base — his final paper proposed Cyc+LLM integration.

entities/douglas-engelbart.title: Douglas Engelbart
entities/douglas-engelbart.summary: American engineer (1925-2013) who invented the mouse, hyperlink, and collaborative computing, inspired by Bush's Memex — his 1968 'Mother of All Demos' previewed modern interactive computing 25 years early.

entities/dspy.title: DSPy
entities/dspy.summary: Declarative Self-improving Python framework that acts as a 'compiler' for LLM prompts, optimizing entire pipelines at compile-time — raised accuracy from 46.2% to 64.0% on prompt evaluation tasks.

entities/edward-feigenbaum.title: Edward Feigenbaum
entities/edward-feigenbaum.summary: American computer scientist (b. 1936), 'father of expert systems,' who led the Stanford Heuristic Programming Project and established that knowledge is more important than inference methods.

entities/elicit.title: Elicit
entities/elicit.summary: AI research assistant purpose-built for academic literature reviews — customizable comparison tables, semantic paper summaries, and structured data extraction from peer-reviewed sources ($10-65/month).

entities/elinor-ostrom.title: Elinor Ostrom
entities/elinor-ostrom.summary: Nobel Prize-winning political economist (1933-2012) whose commons governance framework — originally for natural resources — became foundational for understanding digital knowledge commons governance.

entities/elvis-saravia.title: Elvis Saravia
entities/elvis-saravia.summary: Founder of DAIR.AI Academy who provided the most thorough system architecture analysis of Karpathy's LLM knowledge base, coining the 'four-phase operational cycle' framework.

entities/enterprise-knowledge.title: Enterprise Knowledge (consulting firm)
entities/enterprise-knowledge.summary: Knowledge management consulting firm led by CEO Zach Wahl. Publishes influential annual KM trend reports (proven prescient since 2019). Specializes in semantic layer implementations, taxonomy, and information architecture for enterprise AI initiatives.

entities/eu-ai-act.title: EU AI Act
entities/eu-ai-act.summary: The world's first comprehensive AI regulation — a binding EU law with extraterritorial reach, four risk tiers, penalties up to EUR 35M, and full enforcement beginning August 2, 2026.

entities/eureka-labs.title: Eureka Labs
entities/eureka-labs.summary: Karpathy's AI-native education company (founded July 2024) building LLM101n — a from-scratch LLM course with AI teaching assistants supporting human instructors.

entities/evabyte.title: EvaByte
entities/evabyte.summary: A 6.5B open-source tokenization-free byte-level language model from HKU/SambaNova that matches tokenizer-based models, using multibyte prediction and EVA linear attention.

entities/everlaw.title: Everlaw
entities/everlaw.summary: AI-powered e-discovery and document analysis platform for legal teams — rapidly summarizes and classifies large document volumes for litigation, investigations, and regulatory compliance.

entities/excalidraw.title: Excalidraw (Obsidian Plugin)
entities/excalidraw.summary: The most-downloaded Obsidian community plugin: a full-featured freehand drawing and diagramming tool embedded in the vault for visual thinking alongside notes.

entities/executorch.title: ExecuTorch
entities/executorch.summary: Meta's production on-device inference framework: 50KB base footprint, 12+ hardware backends, reached 1.0 GA in October 2025, serving billions of users across Meta's mobile apps.

entities/faiss.title: FAISS
entities/faiss.summary: Facebook AI Similarity Search -- an open-source library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors, supporting billions of vectors with disk-based indexing.

entities/falkordb.title: FalkorDB
entities/falkordb.summary: Graph database with GraphRAG SDK for performance-critical knowledge graph deployments. Sub-50ms query latency, 90% hallucination reduction vs. traditional RAG, multi-model support (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Groq, Ollama). Self-hosted or cloud deployment.

entities/fei-fei-li.title: Fei-Fei Li
entities/fei-fei-li.summary: Stanford professor, ImageNet creator, and Karpathy's PhD advisor — one of the most influential figures in computer vision and AI.

entities/figma.title: Figma
entities/figma.summary: Collaborative design tool whose 'Figma Make' feature exemplifies AI-native collaboration: natural language prompts + full creative control + AI suggestions awaiting user approval.

entities/fineweb.title: FineWeb
entities/fineweb.summary: HuggingFace's 15T-token open LLM pretraining dataset from 96 CommonCrawl dumps — the largest publicly available clean dataset, with FineWeb-Edu (1.3T educational tokens) and FineWeb-2 (1,000+ languages) variants.

entities/firecrawl.title: Firecrawl
entities/firecrawl.summary: AI-focused web scraping API by Mendable.ai: converts websites to LLM-ready markdown/JSON via single API call, handles JS rendering and anti-bot, six modes (scrape/crawl/map/search/interact/agent), MCP Server for LLM integration.

entities/flashattention.title: FlashAttention
entities/flashattention.summary: IO-aware exact attention algorithm by Tri Dao reducing memory from O(N^2) to O(N) via tiling — now the default attention implementation in PyTorch, JAX, and all major LLM frameworks, with v3 achieving 75% H100 utilization.

entities/freshwiki.title: FreshWiki
entities/freshwiki.summary: An evaluation dataset of recent Wikipedia articles created after LLM training cutoffs, introduced by the STORM project to prevent data leakage in automated wiki generation benchmarks.

entities/future-of-life-institute.title: Future of Life Institute
entities/future-of-life-institute.summary: Research organization publishing the AI Safety Index — an independent evaluation of AI companies across 33 indicators in 6 safety domains, with grades from F to C+.

entities/g-eval.title: G-Eval
entities/g-eval.summary: LLM-as-a-Judge scoring method using chain-of-thought reasoning before evaluation; generates evaluation steps from task criteria, produces scores (1-5), and optionally normalizes via token probabilities for stability.

entities/gemma.title: Gemma (Google)
entities/gemma.summary: Google's open-weight SLM family — Gemma 3 4B offers 128K context and multimodal vision in 3GB VRAM; Gemma 270M runs 25 conversations on 0.75% phone battery.

entities/github-copilot.title: GitHub Copilot
entities/github-copilot.summary: The industry-standard AI coding assistant at $10-21/mo, used by 90% of Fortune 100, offering inline completions, chat, and agent mode across VS Code, JetBrains, and Neovim — pragmatic and frictionless but limited in reasoning depth.

entities/glean.title: Glean
entities/glean.summary: AI-powered enterprise search platform built on Enterprise Graph architecture. Integrates with 100+ SaaS apps. Series F funding ($150M). Combines semantic search, RAG, permission-aware access, code intelligence, and agentic workflows. Market leader in unified enterprise search.

entities/google-adk.title: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
entities/google-adk.summary: Google's framework for building AI agents with integrated support for six protocols: MCP (tools), A2A (agent collaboration), UCP (commerce), AP2 (payments), A2UI (dynamic UI), AG-UI (streaming).

entities/google-notebooklm.title: Google NotebookLM
entities/google-notebooklm.summary: Google's AI notebook product that allows users to upload documents and ask questions -- the closest existing product to Karpathy's vision, but lacking persistent wiki compilation and the filing loop.

entities/gpt.title: GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer)
entities/gpt.summary: OpenAI's decoder-only transformer family using causal language modeling — from GPT-1 (117M, 2018) to GPT-3 (175B, 2020) to GPT-4, establishing the decoder-only paradigm as the dominant LLM architecture.

entities/graphite.title: Graphite
entities/graphite.summary: AI code review tool with 96% positive feedback rate and 55% developer action rate (exceeding 49% for human reviewers) — launched October 2025 with stacked PR support and conversational AI interface.

entities/graphiti.title: Graphiti
entities/graphiti.summary: An open-source framework by Zep for building temporal context graphs where facts have validity windows, designed for AI agents operating in dynamic environments.

entities/hax-toolkit.title: HAX Toolkit (Human-AI Experience)
entities/hax-toolkit.summary: Microsoft Research's design library for human-AI interaction — provides guidelines and patterns for first-run experience, during interaction, error handling, and long-term engagement in AI products.

entities/helm.title: HELM (Holistic Evaluation of Language Models)
entities/helm.summary: The most comprehensive academic LLM evaluation framework: 42 scenarios, 7 evaluation metrics, 16+ models with standardized methodology and public leaderboard.

entities/ibm-research.title: IBM Research
entities/ibm-research.summary: IBM's AI research division: developed predictive LLM routing using HELM benchmarks, demonstrating GPT-4-matching quality at 5 cents/query savings through intelligent model selection.

entities/instructgpt.title: InstructGPT
entities/instructgpt.summary: OpenAI's 2022 paper that demonstrated the three-step RLHF pipeline (SFT, reward model training, PPO) at scale, producing a 1.3B parameter model preferred over the 175B GPT-3 -- the direct precursor to ChatGPT.

entities/instructor.title: Instructor
entities/instructor.summary: The most popular Python library for structured LLM extraction (3M+ monthly downloads) — uses Pydantic models with automatic validation and retry across 15+ providers.

entities/jason-wei.title: Jason Wei
entities/jason-wei.summary: Google Brain / DeepMind researcher, first author of the foundational Chain-of-Thought Prompting paper (2022) and co-first author of the Emergent Abilities paper (2022), two of the most influential works in LLM reasoning.

entities/jina-reader.title: Jina Reader API
entities/jina-reader.summary: Jina's Reader API converts any URL to LLM-friendly markdown by prefixing r.jina.ai/ — uses headless Chrome + Readability + Turndown, with optional ReaderLM v2 neural engine.

entities/john-mccarthy.title: John McCarthy
entities/john-mccarthy.summary: American computer scientist (1927-2011) who coined 'artificial intelligence' (1956), invented LISP (1958), proposed the Advice Taker, and championed logic-based AI — founding the 'neat' tradition.

entities/julie-zhuo.title: Julie Zhuo
entities/julie-zhuo.summary: Former VP Design at Facebook/Meta; influential product design voice arguing that conversational UI was a breakthrough of obviousness but has five critical limitations, with AI personalization as the billion-dollar opportunity.

entities/karma-framework.title: KARMA
entities/karma-framework.summary: NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight paper: 9-agent LLM framework for automated knowledge graph enrichment from unstructured text, achieving 83.1% accuracy and 38,230 new entities from 1,200 PubMed papers.

entities/karma.title: KARMA
entities/karma.summary: A NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight paper presenting a nine-agent LLM framework for automated knowledge graph enrichment from unstructured scientific text.

entities/kggen.title: KGGen
entities/kggen.summary: Open-source Python library for extracting knowledge graphs from text via a 3-stage pipeline (generate, aggregate, cluster), achieving 66% on the MINE benchmark — 18% above GraphRAG.

entities/langchain.title: LangChain
entities/langchain.summary: Open-source LLM application framework: document loaders, RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter for chunking, chains (Stuff/Refine/MapReduce) for document processing, and extensive LLM provider integrations.

entities/langgraph.title: LangGraph
entities/langgraph.summary: LangChain's framework for building stateful, multi-step LLM applications as state machines with cycles, conditional logic, and agent loops — the primary implementation platform for agentic RAG.

entities/lilian-weng.title: Lilian Weng
entities/lilian-weng.summary: OpenAI researcher and author of Lil'Log, producing definitive technical surveys on topics including reward hacking, agents, prompt engineering, and LLM training -- widely cited in the ML community.

entities/llama-cpp.title: llama.cpp
entities/llama-cpp.summary: C/C++ LLM inference engine — foundation for Ollama; supports GGUF format, 1.5-8 bit quantization, CPU+GPU splitting; runs on every platform from phones to servers.

entities/llama.title: Llama
entities/llama.summary: Meta's open-source LLM family, with Llama 3.1 8B used in the Decoding AI second-brain RAG pipeline as the fine-tuned summarization model.

entities/llamaindex.title: LlamaIndex
entities/llamaindex.summary: Leading RAG framework with composable ingestion pipeline: SimpleDirectoryReader + LlamaParse + LlamaHub loaders, node parsers for chunking, cache-optimized transformations, docstore deduplication, and automatic vector store integration.

entities/llamaparse.title: LlamaParse
entities/llamaparse.summary: LlamaIndex's managed PDF parsing API: best-in-class for complex tables and figures, integrates natively with LlamaIndex ingestion pipeline, proprietary cloud service.

entities/llm-c.title: llm.c
entities/llm-c.summary: LLM training in pure C/CUDA: ~3,000 lines reproducing GPT-2 (124M) in 90 minutes for $20, running 7% faster than PyTorch — Karpathy's proof that frameworks are optional.

entities/lm-studio.title: LM Studio
entities/lm-studio.summary: Desktop GUI application for local LLM inference — polished model browser, Vulkan offloading for integrated GPUs, best entry point for non-technical users.

entities/logseq.title: Logseq
entities/logseq.summary: Open-source, local-first outliner with block-based architecture, bidirectional linking, and advanced querying — positioned between Obsidian (markdown-first) and Roam (cloud-first) in the PKM tool landscape.

entities/lost-in-the-middle-paper.title: Lost in the Middle (Paper)
entities/lost-in-the-middle-paper.summary: Liu et al. (Stanford/UC Berkeley, TACL 2023): landmark paper documenting the U-shaped performance curve where LLMs perform best on beginning/end information and >30% worse on middle-positioned content.

entities/maggie-appleton.title: Maggie Appleton
entities/maggie-appleton.summary: Designer, illustrator, and anthropologist who compiled the definitive history and pattern language of digital gardens — identifying six core principles that distinguish gardens from traditional blogs.

entities/magic-ltm.title: Magic / LTM-2-Mini
entities/magic-ltm.summary: Magic's LTM-2-Mini: 100M token context model using a novel sequence-dimension algorithm 1,000x cheaper than standard attention, requiring a fraction of one H100 vs 638 for Llama 405B.

entities/markdowndb.title: MarkdownDB
entities/markdowndb.summary: Open-source JS library that indexes markdown files into SQLite for SQL/JSON querying — files remain on disk as plain text, with the database as a derived index.

entities/markitdown.title: MarkItDown (Microsoft)
entities/markitdown.summary: Microsoft's open-source Python tool for converting PDFs, Office docs, images, audio, and web content to markdown — designed for LLM ingestion pipelines.

entities/marp.title: Marp
entities/marp.summary: A markdown-based presentation framework used within Obsidian to render LLM-generated slide decks as one of the multi-format output options in the knowledge base workflow.

entities/marvin-minsky.title: Marvin Minsky
entities/marvin-minsky.summary: American cognitive scientist (1927-2016), co-founder of MIT AI Lab, who developed frame theory for knowledge representation and co-authored 'Perceptrons' (1969) which temporarily halted neural network research.

entities/matplotlib.title: Matplotlib
entities/matplotlib.summary: A Python plotting library used in the LLM-KB workflow to generate data visualizations that are saved as images and viewed within Obsidian alongside wiki articles.

entities/mdx.title: MDX
entities/mdx.summary: Authoring format that blends markdown with JSX components — 'Markdown for the component era' — with zero runtime, compiling to JavaScript at build time.

entities/med-palm.title: Med-PaLM
entities/med-palm.summary: Google's medical LLM family — Med-PaLM 2 exceeded baseline models by 19% on MultiMedQA, reaching expert-level performance on medical licensing exams and clinical QA benchmarks.

entities/megatron-lm.title: Megatron-LM
entities/megatron-lm.summary: NVIDIA's framework for training large transformer models, pioneering efficient tensor parallelism (splitting weight matrices within layers) and interleaved pipeline parallelism. Often combined with DeepSpeed as Megatron-DeepSpeed.

entities/memex.title: Memex
entities/memex.summary: Vannevar Bush's 1945 vision of a personal knowledge device with associative cross-referencing -- the conceptual ancestor of hypertext, wikis, and LLM-maintained knowledge bases.

entities/memgpt-letta.title: MemGPT / Letta
entities/memgpt-letta.summary: Open-source platform for stateful LLM agents with OS-inspired virtual context management; LLM self-manages memory hierarchy (core/recall/archival) through tool calls.

entities/meta-llama.title: Meta Llama
entities/meta-llama.summary: Meta's open-weight LLM family — Llama 4 introduced MoE architecture with Scout (10M token context), Maverick (multimodal), and Behemoth (2T params, teacher model).

entities/metr.title: METR
entities/metr.summary: AI safety research organization that conducted the landmark RCT finding experienced open-source developers are 19% slower with AI tools — the most rigorous empirical challenge to AI productivity claims.

entities/micrograd.title: micrograd
entities/micrograd.summary: Karpathy's educational autograd engine: ~100 lines of Python implementing backpropagation over a dynamically built DAG, with a ~50-line neural net library — the most accessible introduction to how deep learning actually works.

entities/microsoft-graphrag.title: Microsoft GraphRAG
entities/microsoft-graphrag.summary: Open-source modular graph-based RAG system from Microsoft Research that builds knowledge graphs from text using LLM extraction, Leiden community detection, and hierarchical summarization.

entities/microsoft-phi.title: Microsoft Phi Models
entities/microsoft-phi.summary: Microsoft Research model family (phi-1 through phi-4) demonstrating that 'textbook quality' synthetic data enables small models (1.3B-14B) to rival or surpass models 10-25x larger.

entities/microsoft-research.title: Microsoft Research
entities/microsoft-research.summary: Developed GraphRAG — a knowledge-graph-based approach to RAG that constructs community hierarchies for holistic query answering, now available as open-source on GitHub and integrated into Azure.

entities/minbpe.title: minbpe
entities/minbpe.summary: Karpathy's minimal, clean reference implementation of BPE tokenization — the most widely-cited educational codebase for understanding LLM tokenization.

entities/minhash-lsh.title: MinHash LSH
entities/minhash-lsh.summary: Probabilistic algorithm combining MinHash signatures with Locality-Sensitive Hashing to efficiently detect near-duplicate documents at trillion-token scale — the standard deduplication method for LLM training data.

entities/mixtral.title: Mixtral 8x7B
entities/mixtral.summary: Mistral AI's 2023 open-weight MoE model: 47B total parameters, 8 experts with 2 active per token (~12B FLOPs), outperforming Llama 2 70B while running at 12B-model speed.

entities/mlx.title: MLX
entities/mlx.summary: Apple's open-source ML framework for Apple Silicon — exploits unified memory for zero-copy inference; leads throughput on <14B models; supports on-device LoRA fine-tuning.

entities/mmlu.title: MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding)
entities/mmlu.summary: The most widely-cited LLM knowledge benchmark: 15,908 multiple-choice questions across 57 subjects from elementary math to professional law — now saturated above 90% for frontier models.

entities/mongodb.title: MongoDB
entities/mongodb.summary: A document database with vector search capabilities used as the storage and retrieval backend in the Decoding AI production RAG pipeline for second-brain AI assistants.

entities/mozilla-readability.title: Mozilla Readability (Readability.js)
entities/mozilla-readability.summary: Mozilla's standalone JavaScript library for extracting article content from web pages via a 7-heuristic, 6-stage DOM scoring pipeline — powers Firefox Reader View and underpins Jina Reader API.

entities/mt-bench.title: MT-Bench
entities/mt-bench.summary: Fixed 80-question multi-turn benchmark spanning 8 categories (writing, roleplay, extraction, reasoning, math, coding, knowledge, stem), created by LMSYS for evaluating LLM conversation quality.

entities/mteb.title: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark)
entities/mteb.summary: The standard benchmark for evaluating text embedding models: 8 task categories across 56+ English datasets (MMTEB: 131 tasks, 250+ languages), hosted on Hugging Face with a continuously updated leaderboard.

entities/nanogpt.title: nanoGPT
entities/nanogpt.summary: Karpathy's simplest, fastest GPT training repository: reproduces GPT-2 (124M) on OpenWebText in ~4 days on 8xA100, serving as both educational reference and practical training tool.

entities/nathan-lambert.title: Nathan Lambert
entities/nathan-lambert.summary: AI researcher and author of the RLHF Book — the most comprehensive public resource on reinforcement learning from human feedback, covering preference data collection, reward modeling, and alignment.

entities/nemotron-cc.title: Nemotron-CC
entities/nemotron-cc.summary: NVIDIA's 6.3T-token dataset (4.4T real + 1.9T synthetic) using classifier ensembling and differentiated synthetic generation — 4x more unique tokens than DCLM while exceeding Llama 3.1 8B on MMLU.

entities/neo4j.title: Neo4j
entities/neo4j.summary: A native graph database used as the backend for Graphiti's temporal context graphs, providing mature graph query and visualization capabilities.

entities/neural-turing-machine.title: Neural Turing Machine
entities/neural-turing-machine.summary: Alex Graves et al. (2014) architecture coupling a neural network controller with external memory via differentiable soft attention — the foundational work connecting attention mechanisms to external memory, enabling networks to learn algorithmic tasks like copy, sort, and associative recall.

entities/niklas-luhmann.title: Niklas Luhmann
entities/niklas-luhmann.summary: German sociologist (1927-1998) who developed the Zettelkasten method, producing 70 books and 400+ articles using a system of 90,000 interconnected index cards that he described as a 'communication partner.'

entities/nist-ai-rmf.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
entities/nist-ai-rmf.summary: Voluntary U.S. framework for AI risk management organized around four functions (Govern/Map/Measure/Manage); widely referenced as a global baseline by regulators and standards bodies.

entities/notion.title: Notion
entities/notion.summary: Flexible block-based workspace with 100M+ users, ranked #1 for knowledge bases on G2. Expanding from PKM into enterprise work OS with autonomous AI Agent, Enterprise Search, Calendar, Mail, and Sites. Base plan includes AI; $10/user/month. Competes with Confluence (structured wiki) and SharePoint (compliance-focused).

entities/novartis.title: Novartis
entities/novartis.summary: Pharmaceutical company using graph databases to link internal research data with external research abstracts, connecting genes, diseases, and compounds to accelerate drug discovery. One of the most notable enterprise knowledge graph deployments.

entities/obsidian-copilot.title: Obsidian Copilot
entities/obsidian-copilot.summary: The #1 downloaded AI plugin for Obsidian (100K+ users): model-agnostic chat assistant with vault RAG, project workspaces, diff-preview composer, and all data stored as plain markdown.

entities/obsidian-web-clipper.title: Obsidian Web Clipper
entities/obsidian-web-clipper.summary: A browser extension for converting web articles into markdown files for ingestion into the raw/ directory of an LLM knowledge base.

entities/obsidian.title: Obsidian
entities/obsidian.summary: A local-first, markdown-based knowledge management platform with 1.5M users, 2,700+ plugins, and a 'file over app' philosophy — serves as the frontend IDE for LLM-maintained wikis.

entities/ollama.title: Ollama
entities/ollama.summary: Most popular local LLM tool (150K+ GitHub stars) — abstracts llama.cpp into Docker-like experience with Modelfiles, OpenAI-compatible API, and cross-platform GPU support.

entities/ontogpt.title: OntoGPT
entities/ontogpt.summary: Python package for ontology-grounded information extraction using LLMs and the SPIRES zero-shot method — extracts structured data aligned to established biomedical ontologies.

entities/openai-codex.title: OpenAI Codex
entities/openai-codex.summary: OpenAI's agentic coding tool -- cloud sandbox-based, zero-dependency Rust CLI, 1,000+ tok/s on Cerebras hardware -- excelling at rapid prototyping and terminal-heavy workflows with 56.8% SWE-bench Pro and 77.3% Terminal-Bench.

entities/openai-embeddings.title: OpenAI Embeddings
entities/openai-embeddings.summary: OpenAI's embedding API models: text-embedding-ada-002 (1536 dims, legacy), text-embedding-3-small/large (native Matryoshka, up to 3072 dims) — widely used but increasingly matched by open-source alternatives.

entities/openai.title: OpenAI
entities/openai.summary: AI research company behind GPT-4, o1, and o3 reasoning models -- pioneers of process reward models (PRM800K), scaled reinforcement learning for reasoning, and test-time search with deliberative alignment.

entities/openfactcheck.title: OpenFactCheck
entities/openfactcheck.summary: Open-source unified framework for LLM factuality evaluation with three modules: ResponseEvaluator (claim-level fact-checking), LLMEvaluator (FactQA, 6,480 examples), and FactCheckerEvaluator (FactBench, 4,507 annotated examples).

entities/owasp.title: OWASP
entities/owasp.summary: Open Worldwide Application Security Project — ranked prompt injection as the #1 AI security risk in its 2025 Top 10 for LLMs.

entities/pandoc.title: Pandoc
entities/pandoc.summary: Universal document converter (Haskell, GPL) that converts between 40+ formats via a markdown-centric AST — maintained since 2006 by John MacFarlane.

entities/perplexity-ai.title: Perplexity AI
entities/perplexity-ai.summary: AI-powered research tool providing citation-backed answers with real-time web search; gold standard for fast, multi-source discovery; Deep Research mode autonomously synthesizes dozens of sources.

entities/pgvector.title: pgvector
entities/pgvector.summary: A PostgreSQL extension for vector similarity search, widely regarded as sufficient for most team-scale retrieval use cases without requiring dedicated vector database infrastructure.

entities/phi.title: Phi (Microsoft)
entities/phi.summary: Microsoft's SLM family — Phi-4 (14B) beats GPT-4o on MATH/GPQA with 84.8% MMLU; Phi-4-mini (3.8B) runs on 3GB VRAM with 128K context.

entities/philip-gage.title: Philip Gage
entities/philip-gage.summary: Inventor of the Byte Pair Encoding algorithm (1994), originally designed for text compression and later adapted for LLM tokenization.

entities/pinecone.title: Pinecone
entities/pinecone.summary: Fully managed vector database service: proprietary indexing, sub-10ms latency at tens of billions of vectors, SOC 2 + HIPAA + ISO 27001, with Pinecone Assistant for integrated RAG (GA January 2025).

entities/playwright.title: Playwright
entities/playwright.summary: Microsoft's cross-browser automation framework — the modern headless browser of choice for web scraping, supporting Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, with auto-waiting, parallel execution, and stealth capabilities.

entities/prometheus.title: Prometheus
entities/prometheus.summary: Open-source LLM evaluator fine-tuned on 100K GPT-4 feedback samples (based on Llama-2-Chat); achieves 0.897 Pearson correlation with human judgments using explicit rubrics and reference answers.

entities/prompt-engineering-guide.title: Prompt Engineering Guide (DAIR.AI)
entities/prompt-engineering-guide.summary: Comprehensive open-source resource at promptingguide.ai maintained by DAIR.AI, covering all major prompting techniques with research citations and examples — the de facto reference for the field.

entities/pydantic.title: Pydantic
entities/pydantic.summary: Python data validation library using type hints — the de facto standard for defining LLM extraction schemas, powering Instructor, Pydantic AI, LangChain structured output, and Simon Willison's LLM.

entities/pymupdf.title: PyMuPDF
entities/pymupdf.summary: Fastest Python PDF parser (0.12s markdown output): PyMuPDF4LLM variant optimized for LLM ingestion with layout analysis and semantic understanding; most consistent recall among rule-based tools; AGPL/commercial license.

entities/qdrant.title: Qdrant
entities/qdrant.summary: Open-source vector database written in Rust: HNSW indexing, richest feature set (hybrid search, geo-spatial, multi-vector, sparse vectors), 326 QPS, available as self-hosted, managed cloud, or hybrid deployment.

entities/qwen.title: Qwen
entities/qwen.summary: Alibaba's open-source LLM family — Qwen 3.5 (397B MoE) leads reasoning benchmarks; Qwen 2.5 Coder (88.4% HumanEval) beats GPT-4; small variants (4B) rival 72B models.

entities/qwen3-vl.title: Qwen3-VL
entities/qwen3-vl.summary: Alibaba's flagship open-source VLM (235B params, 22B active MoE): rivals GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro with 256K-1M context, multilingual OCR (32 languages), and visual agent capabilities.

entities/ragas.title: RAGAS (Retrieval Augmented Generation Assessment)
entities/ragas.summary: The leading open-source framework for reference-free evaluation of RAG pipelines, providing metrics for faithfulness, context precision/recall, answer relevancy, and synthetic test data generation.

entities/raptor-paper.title: RAPTOR Paper (ICLR 2024)
entities/raptor-paper.summary: ICLR 2024 paper by Sarthi, Abdullah et al. introducing RAPTOR — recursive tree construction via GMM clustering and abstractive summarization for multi-level retrieval, achieving 20% improvement on QuALITY.

entities/reader-lm.title: Reader-LM (Jina)
entities/reader-lm.summary: Jina's 1.5B-parameter specialized language model for HTML-to-markdown conversion — outperforms GPT-4o (ROUGE-L 0.86 vs 0.43) by treating the task as selective-copy, with 512K token context and 29-language support.

entities/redis.title: Redis
entities/redis.summary: In-memory data platform used for LLM semantic caching: Redis LangCache stores query embeddings alongside responses, achieving 73% cost reduction with sub-millisecond vector search across millions of entries.

entities/retro.title: RETRO (Retrieval-Enhanced Transformer)
entities/retro.summary: DeepMind's 7.5B parameter model matching GPT-3 (185B) by augmenting a transformer with a 2-trillion-token retrieval database accessed via chunked cross-attention — decoupling factual memorization from language reasoning.

entities/roam-research.title: Roam Research
entities/roam-research.summary: The note-taking tool that popularized bidirectional linking in 2020, treating every block as a referenceable node in a personal knowledge graph — positioned as 'a note-taking tool for networked thought.'

entities/rome-memit.title: ROME and MEMIT
entities/rome-memit.summary: Pioneering knowledge editing methods: ROME makes rank-one MLP modifications for single fact edits; MEMIT scales to thousands of simultaneous edits across transformer layers.

entities/sam-gallagher.title: Sam Gallagher
entities/sam-gallagher.summary: Developer who built the Knowledge Graph Kit, an open-source MCP server using SQLite and ChromaDB, as a structure-first alternative to markdown-based personal knowledge management.

entities/sapphire-ventures.title: Sapphire Ventures
entities/sapphire-ventures.summary: Enterprise VC firm that developed the 5-D framework (Design, Data, Domain Expertise, Dynamism, Distribution) for evaluating AI-native applications, tracking $8.5B invested in GenAI-native apps.

entities/scite.title: Scite
entities/scite.summary: Citation analysis tool with 1.2 billion citation statements from 187M+ articles — shows whether papers are cited supportively, contrastingly, or merely mentioned, enabling research claim verification.

entities/scrapy.title: Scrapy
entities/scrapy.summary: Python's premier web crawling framework — 2,500 pages/min throughput, 1,000 concurrent requests via Twisted async, with built-in pipelines, retry logic, and rate limiting for large-scale scraping.

entities/sebastian-raschka.title: Sebastian Raschka
entities/sebastian-raschka.summary: ML researcher and educator; author of 'Build a Large Language Model From Scratch' and popular BPE implementation tutorials.

entities/sentence-transformers.title: Sentence Transformers
entities/sentence-transformers.summary: The leading open-source Python library for text embeddings (Hugging Face): provides pretrained models (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, mpnet), training utilities (MatryoshkaLoss, contrastive losses), and a simple encode() API.

entities/sglang.title: SGLang
entities/sglang.summary: Open-source LLM serving framework and 2026 throughput leader: RadixAttention achieves 85-95% cache hit rates and 16,215 tok/s on H100, beating vLLM by 29% for multi-turn and agentic workloads.

entities/shape-of-ai.title: The Shape of AI
entities/shape-of-ai.summary: Community-maintained catalog of 57 AI UX design patterns organized into six categories (Wayfinders, Prompt Actions, Tuners, Governors, Trust Builders, Identifiers) — the most comprehensive open taxonomy of AI interaction patterns.

entities/sharepoint.title: SharePoint
entities/sharepoint.summary: Microsoft's enterprise content management platform serving 190M+ users across 200,000 organizations. Granular permissions (site, list, item levels), extensive compliance certifications (HIPAA). Requires Microsoft 365 Copilot ($30/user/month) for AI features. Best fit for regulated enterprises in the Microsoft ecosystem.

entities/simon-willison.title: Simon Willison
entities/simon-willison.summary: Creator of Datasette and the LLM CLI tool — champions structured data extraction as 'the single most commercially valuable application of LLMs.'

entities/smart-connections.title: Smart Connections
entities/smart-connections.summary: Leading free Obsidian AI plugin using RAG to enable conversational queries across the entire vault — works with local (Ollama) and cloud models.

entities/sqlite.title: SQLite
entities/sqlite.summary: A lightweight, serverless relational database used as the structural storage layer in Gallagher's Knowledge Graph Kit for personal knowledge management.

entities/steph-ango.title: Steph Ango
entities/steph-ango.summary: CEO of Obsidian, designer, and writer — articulated the 'file over app' philosophy, vault separation pattern, and a bottom-up approach to PKM with fractal journaling.

entities/storm.title: STORM
entities/storm.summary: A research system for automated Wikipedia-style article creation using multi-perspective question-asking and retrieval-based outline synthesis.

entities/streamingllm.title: StreamingLLM
entities/streamingllm.summary: MIT HAN Lab framework enabling LLMs to generate over infinite-length sequences by preserving attention sink tokens plus a rolling KV window — no fine-tuning required, validated across Llama-2, MPT, Falcon, and Pythia up to 4M+ tokens with 22.2x speedup.

entities/surya-ocr.title: Surya OCR
entities/surya-ocr.summary: High-performance multilingual OCR toolkit by Vik Paruchuri: YOLOv5 text detection, Transformer recognition across 90+ languages, graph neural network layout analysis, 15-20% improvement over commercial tools on complex tables.

entities/swe-bench.title: SWE-bench
entities/swe-bench.summary: The dominant benchmark for AI software engineering agents -- real GitHub issues from production Python repos -- showing 59% improvement from 48.5% (GPT-4, 2023) to 80.8% (Opus 4.6, 2026) in under two years.

entities/switch-transformer.title: Switch Transformer
entities/switch-transformer.summary: Google's 2021 MoE model scaling to 1.6T parameters with 2048 experts using simplified single-expert routing — 4x pretraining speedup over T5-XXL, demonstrating MoE scaling viability.

entities/t5.title: T5 (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer)
entities/t5.summary: Google's 2019 encoder-decoder transformer converting all NLP tasks to text-to-text format — 220M to 11B parameters, trained on C4 with span denoising, basis for Switch Transformer.

entities/ted-nelson.title: Ted Nelson
entities/ted-nelson.summary: American information technology pioneer (b. 1937) who coined 'hypertext' in 1965, founded Project Xanadu (1960), and envisioned bidirectional links, transclusion, and micropayments decades before the web.

entities/templater.title: Templater
entities/templater.summary: Obsidian's advanced templating plugin (230K+ installs): dynamic variables, JavaScript execution, file manipulation, conditional logic, and user prompts — the automation backbone of power-user workflows.

entities/tesla.title: Tesla
entities/tesla.summary: Electric vehicle and AI company where Karpathy served as Director of AI (2017-2022), leading the Autopilot Vision team — Software 2.0 at industrial scale.

entities/textgrad.title: TextGrad
entities/textgrad.summary: Gradient-based prompt optimization framework that uses natural language feedback instead of numeric scores — published in Nature (2025), excels at instance-level refinement for coding and scientific Q&A.

entities/tiago-forte.title: Tiago Forte
entities/tiago-forte.summary: Productivity consultant and author who created the Building a Second Brain (BASB) methodology, including the PARA organizational system and Progressive Summarization technique — the most popular PKM framework globally.

entities/tiktoken.title: tiktoken
entities/tiktoken.summary: OpenAI's fast BPE tokenizer library, written in Rust with a Python API — the standard tool for counting tokens for GPT models.

entities/trafilatura.title: Trafilatura
entities/trafilatura.summary: The most accurate open-source web text extraction library — Python package combining jusText and Readability algorithms, outputting to markdown/JSON/XML-TEI, used by HuggingFace, IBM, Microsoft Research.

entities/tri-dao.title: Tri Dao
entities/tri-dao.summary: Co-creator of FlashAttention (IO-aware attention optimization) and Mamba (selective state space models) — two of the most impactful systems contributions to modern LLM efficiency.

entities/trl.title: TRL (Transformers Reinforcement Learning)
entities/trl.summary: HuggingFace's library for LLM alignment training, supporting SFT, PPO, DPO, IPO, KTO, and ORPO -- the de facto standard open-source toolkit for preference optimization.

entities/truthfulqa.title: TruthfulQA
entities/truthfulqa.summary: 817-question benchmark testing whether LLMs propagate common misconceptions; notable for revealing that state-of-the-art models score 'surprisingly low on truthfulness.'

entities/unstructured-io.title: Unstructured.io
entities/unstructured-io.summary: Open-source Python library (Apache 2.0) for document ETL: partition() auto-detects 30+ formats, outputs typed semantic elements, four processing strategies, 14.4k GitHub stars, enterprise platform processes 15M pages/hour.

entities/vannevar-bush.title: Vannevar Bush
entities/vannevar-bush.summary: American engineer and science administrator who envisioned the Memex in 1945 -- a proto-hypertext personal knowledge device that prefigured modern LLM knowledge bases by 80 years.

entities/vespa.title: Vespa.ai
entities/vespa.summary: Yahoo's hybrid search engine combining vector, keyword, and metadata search with multi-vector indexing -- described as underappreciated in the HN vector database debate.

entities/vllm.title: vLLM
entities/vllm.summary: Production-grade LLM inference engine using PagedAttention — achieves 793 TPS on A100 (vs Ollama's 41), best for multi-user and enterprise local deployments.

entities/ward-cunningham.title: Ward Cunningham
entities/ward-cunningham.summary: Inventor of the wiki (1995) and creator of Federated Wiki (2011) — which reimagines collaborative knowledge as 'a chorus of voices' with forking rather than consensus.

entities/weaviate.title: Weaviate
entities/weaviate.summary: Cloud-native open-source vector database: highest QPS (791), native hybrid search with alpha parameter and BM25F, generative module for server-side RAG, HIPAA on AWS (2025).

entities/wikidata.title: Wikidata
entities/wikidata.summary: Wikimedia's collaboratively edited structured knowledge base — 100M+ items in semantic triple format, linked to 7,500+ external databases, forming the backbone of federated knowledge graph infrastructure.

entities/wikipedia.title: Wikipedia
entities/wikipedia.summary: The world's largest collaboratively edited encyclopedia (60M+ articles, 300+ languages) — paradigmatic example of collective intelligence and knowledge commons, now navigating the AI crisis of content generation, training data extraction, and declining visits.

entities/yoshua-bengio.title: Yoshua Bengio
entities/yoshua-bengio.summary: Turing Award winner and pioneer of deep learning; chaired the 2026 International AI Safety Report synthesizing evidence from 100+ experts across 30+ countries.

entities/zenml.title: ZenML
entities/zenml.summary: An open-source MLOps pipeline orchestration framework used in the Decoding AI second-brain RAG system to manage offline data processing and training workflows.

entities/zep.title: Zep
entities/zep.summary: The organization behind Graphiti, offering both an open-source temporal context graph engine and enterprise-grade managed infrastructure for AI agent memory.

comparisons/bi-encoder-vs-cross-encoder-.title: Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder vs ColBERT
comparisons/bi-encoder-vs-cross-encoder-.summary: The three neural retrieval architectures compared: bi-encoders (fast, lossy single-vector), cross-encoders (accurate but slow pairwise scoring), and ColBERT (token-level late interaction bridging both) — with speed, accuracy, and storage tradeoffs.

comparisons/bm25-vs-vector-search.title: BM25 vs Vector Search
comparisons/bm25-vs-vector-search.summary: BM25 excels at exact matches (codes, names, identifiers) while vector search captures semantic meaning — production RAG systems should use both via hybrid search for +26-31% NDCG improvement.

comparisons/bpe-vs-wordpiece-vs-unigram.title: BPE vs WordPiece vs Unigram
comparisons/bpe-vs-wordpiece-vs-unigram.summary: Side-by-side comparison of the three dominant subword tokenization algorithms — BPE (frequency-based merging), WordPiece (likelihood-based merging), and Unigram (probabilistic pruning).

comparisons/claude-code-vs-devin.title: Claude Code vs Devin
comparisons/claude-code-vs-devin.summary: Two leading agentic coding tools: Claude Code (terminal-first, $2.5B revenue, 80.9% SWE-bench) vs Devin (sandboxed environment, first autonomous SE agent, $20/month).

comparisons/claude-vs-gpt-vs-gemini.title: Claude vs GPT vs Gemini (2026)
comparisons/claude-vs-gpt-vs-gemini.summary: 2026 frontier model comparison: Claude Opus 4.6 leads coding/writing, GPT-5.4 leads general reasoning, Gemini 3.1 leads math -- no single winner; best strategy combines models per task.

comparisons/codex-vs-claude-code.title: Codex vs Claude Code
comparisons/codex-vs-claude-code.summary: The two dominant AI coding agents compared: Codex excels at speed, terminal workflows, and cost; Claude Code leads in multi-agent orchestration, determinism, and large codebase navigation -- with a recommended hybrid approach.

comparisons/coding-vs-knowledge-work-llm.title: Coding vs Knowledge Work LLM Applications
comparisons/coding-vs-knowledge-work-llm.summary: Comparing LLM applications in code generation vs. knowledge work domains (writing, research, law, medicine, education) — shared patterns, different maturity levels, and the convergence toward knowledge orchestration.

comparisons/compute-optimal-vs-inference.title: Compute-Optimal vs Inference-Optimal Training
comparisons/compute-optimal-vs-inference.summary: Chinchilla-optimal minimizes loss per training FLOP (~20 tokens/param), but inference-optimal overtrains smaller models on far more data (Llama 3: 1,875:1) because training is one-time while inference runs continuously.

comparisons/consensus-vs-federated-vs-ai.title: Consensus vs Federated vs AI Knowledge Systems
comparisons/consensus-vs-federated-vs-ai.summary: Three paradigms for collaborative knowledge creation: Wikipedia's consensus model, Cunningham's federated plurality model, and AI-driven knowledge compilation — compared on authority, diversity, verification, and scalability.

comparisons/context-management-approache.title: Context Management Approaches Compared
comparisons/context-management-approache.summary: Four approaches to the context limit problem compared: compression (fit more in), virtual context (page in/out), infinite context (remove limits architecturally), and context engineering (use less, smarter).

comparisons/conversational-vs-structured.title: Conversational vs Structured vs Hybrid AI UI
comparisons/conversational-vs-structured.summary: Three UI paradigms for AI products compared: conversational (chat) excels at intent expression but fails at refinement; structured (forms/controls) excels at precision but limits expressiveness; hybrid combines both and is the emerging winner.

comparisons/cot-vs-tot-vs-self-consisten.title: CoT vs Tree of Thoughts vs Self-Consistency
comparisons/cot-vs-tot-vs-self-consisten.summary: Three reasoning techniques compared: CoT (single path, cheap), Self-Consistency (multiple independent paths + voting, moderate cost), and ToT (structured tree search with backtracking, expensive) — each suited to different complexity/budget trade-offs.

comparisons/crawl4ai-vs-firecrawl.title: Crawl4AI vs Firecrawl
comparisons/crawl4ai-vs-firecrawl.summary: Open-source Crawl4AI (free, BM25 filtering, self-hosted) vs SaaS Firecrawl (managed infrastructure, pay-per-credit, broader integrations) — both produce LLM-ready markdown from messy web pages.

comparisons/cursor-vs-claude-code-vs-cop.title: Cursor vs Claude Code vs GitHub Copilot
comparisons/cursor-vs-claude-code-vs-cop.summary: The three dominant AI coding tools compared: Cursor (best balanced IDE, $2B ARR), Claude Code (deepest reasoning, 80.8% SWE-bench), GitHub Copilot (lowest friction, 90% Fortune 100) — each optimized for different developer needs.

comparisons/deepspeed-vs-megatron-lm.title: DeepSpeed vs Megatron-LM
comparisons/deepspeed-vs-megatron-lm.summary: Complementary rather than competing: DeepSpeed optimizes memory via ZeRO sharding (easy integration), while Megatron-LM optimizes compute via tensor/pipeline parallelism (requires code changes). Combined as Megatron-DeepSpeed for frontier training.

comparisons/dense-vs-moe-transformers.title: Dense vs MoE Transformers
comparisons/dense-vs-moe-transformers.summary: Dense transformers use all parameters per token; MoE activates a fraction via routing — MoE achieves 4x pretraining speedup and frontier performance but requires full-model memory and load balancing.

comparisons/encoder-only-vs-decoder-only.title: Encoder-Only vs Decoder-Only vs Encoder-Decoder Transformers
comparisons/encoder-only-vs-decoder-only.summary: Three transformer variant families: BERT (encoder-only, bidirectional understanding), GPT (decoder-only, autoregressive generation — now dominant), T5 (encoder-decoder, flexible text-to-text) — with architecture, training, and use case differences.

comparisons/few-shot-vs-zero-shot.title: Few-Shot vs Zero-Shot Prompting
comparisons/few-shot-vs-zero-shot.summary: Zero-shot is simpler and cheaper (try first); few-shot is more reliable for format control and edge cases (3-5 examples). Research shows few-shot format matters more than label accuracy.

comparisons/fine-tuning-vs-context-windo.title: Fine-Tuning vs. Context Window
comparisons/fine-tuning-vs-context-windo.summary: Comparing two strategies for giving LLMs domain knowledge: fine-tuning (encoding knowledge in model weights) vs. context window retrieval (loading knowledge at query time).

comparisons/fineweb-vs-dclm-vs-nemotron-.title: FineWeb vs DCLM vs Nemotron-CC
comparisons/fineweb-vs-dclm-vs-nemotron-.summary: The three leading open LLM pretraining datasets compared: FineWeb prioritizes scale (15T tokens), DCLM prioritizes rigorous filtering (2T tokens, 64% MMLU), and Nemotron-CC combines both with synthetic augmentation (6.3T tokens, 70.3% MMLU).

comparisons/gptq-vs-awq-vs-gguf.title: GPTQ vs AWQ vs GGUF
comparisons/gptq-vs-awq-vs-gguf.summary: Three dominant LLM quantization methods: GPTQ (GPU default, largest ecosystem), GGUF (CPU/Apple-friendly via llama.cpp), AWQ (best speed-quality balance via activation-aware compression).

comparisons/heuristic-vs-model-based-fil.title: Heuristic vs Model-Based Filtering
comparisons/heuristic-vs-model-based-fil.summary: Heuristic filters (rule-based) handle obvious noise cheaply but miss subtle quality differences; model-based filters (fastText, LLM scorers) capture quality nuances and dominate performance — the decisive finding from DCLM.

comparisons/heuristic-vs-neural-content-.title: Heuristic vs Neural Content Extraction
comparisons/heuristic-vs-neural-content-.summary: Heuristic extraction (Readability, Trafilatura) is fast, free, and works on 90%+ of pages; neural extraction (Reader-LM) achieves higher quality (ROUGE-L 0.86 vs ~0.7) but requires GPU — the choice depends on scale, accuracy needs, and infrastructure.

comparisons/kge-vs-llm-for-knowledge-gra.title: Knowledge Graph Embeddings vs LLMs for Knowledge Graph Tasks
comparisons/kge-vs-llm-for-knowledge-gra.summary: Traditional KGE methods (TransE, ComplEx) vs LLM-based approaches for knowledge graph completion: LLMs dramatically outperform on multi-hop reasoning (F1 0.98 vs 0.61) but KGE retains advantages in efficiency and interpretability.

comparisons/knowledge-editing-vs-fine-tu.title: Knowledge Editing vs. Fine-Tuning
comparisons/knowledge-editing-vs-fine-tu.summary: Knowledge editing (ROME/MEMIT) is surgical and cheap for individual facts but degrades with sequential edits; fine-tuning is broader but expensive — use editing for corrections, fine-tuning for domain adaptation.

comparisons/knowledge-graph-vs-vector-da.title: Knowledge Graph vs Vector Database
comparisons/knowledge-graph-vs-vector-da.summary: Knowledge graphs provide explainability, governance, and multi-hop reasoning; vector databases provide semantic search and fast prototyping; the optimal enterprise approach combines both in a hybrid architecture.

comparisons/knowledge-graph-vs-wiki.title: Knowledge Graph vs. Wiki
comparisons/knowledge-graph-vs-wiki.summary: Comparing formal knowledge graphs (nodes/edges with typed relationships) against flat markdown wikis (files with wikilinks) as substrates for LLM-maintained knowledge bases.

comparisons/llm-judge-vs-human-evaluatio.title: LLM-as-Judge vs Human Evaluation
comparisons/llm-judge-vs-human-evaluatio.summary: LLM judges achieve 80-85% human agreement and enable sub-minute evaluation at sub-$10 cost, but exhibit systematic biases and struggle with factuality; human evaluation remains essential for defining criteria, edge cases, and safety-critical decisions.

comparisons/local-vs-cloud-knowledge-bas.title: Local vs Cloud Knowledge Base
comparisons/local-vs-cloud-knowledge-bas.summary: Cloud KB (Claude API) offers superior reasoning for complex compilation; local KB (Ollama + open models) offers privacy, offline, zero cost — hybrid approach likely optimal.

comparisons/lora-vs-qlora.title: LoRA vs. QLoRA
comparisons/lora-vs-qlora.summary: LoRA (16-bit adapters, 90-95% quality, 16GB for 7B) vs. QLoRA (4-bit quantized base, 80-90% quality, 6GB for 7B) — choose LoRA for production, QLoRA for experimentation.

comparisons/manual-pkm-vs-llm-pkm.title: Manual PKM vs. LLM-Maintained PKM
comparisons/manual-pkm-vs-llm-pkm.summary: Comparing traditional human-authored personal knowledge management (Zettelkasten, Notion, Obsidian notes) with LLM-maintained knowledge bases where the AI authors and organizes all content.

comparisons/manual-vs-ai-pkm.title: Manual PKM vs AI-Maintained PKM
comparisons/manual-vs-ai-pkm.summary: The four stages of PKM evolution compared: Manual (human writes everything), AI-assisted (AI helps with individual tasks), AI-maintained (LLM compiles and links), and Agentic (AI proactively monitors and acts) — tradeoffs in control, quality, scalability, and human role.

comparisons/manual-vs-automated-prompt-o.title: Manual vs Automated Prompt Optimization
comparisons/manual-vs-automated-prompt-o.summary: Manual prompt crafting vs automated optimization (DSPy, TextGrad, Self-Refine): automated approaches achieve 20-64% improvements but add complexity and cost — best combined as a hybrid.

comparisons/markdown-vs-proprietary-form.title: Markdown vs Proprietary Document Formats
comparisons/markdown-vs-proprietary-form.summary: Systematic comparison of markdown against proprietary formats (Word, Notion, Evernote) across longevity, AI-readability, version control, portability, and queryability.

comparisons/mcp-vs-function-calling.title: MCP vs Function Calling
comparisons/mcp-vs-function-calling.summary: MCP is a provider-agnostic client-server protocol for production tool integration; function calling is a simple, provider-specific mechanism best for prototyping. MCP wins on security, portability, and scalability; function calling wins on setup speed.

comparisons/mha-vs-gqa-vs-mqa.title: MHA vs GQA vs MQA
comparisons/mha-vs-gqa-vs-mqa.summary: Multi-Head Attention (max quality, max KV cache) vs Grouped Query Attention (near-MHA quality, 4-8x less KV cache) vs Multi-Query Attention (fastest, quality loss): GQA is the dominant choice for production LLMs since 2023.

comparisons/mlx-vs-llamacpp.title: MLX vs llama.cpp
comparisons/mlx-vs-llamacpp.summary: MLX wins throughput on <14B models (+21-87%) on Apple Silicon; llama.cpp wins for large models (CPU+GPU split), cross-platform, and fine-grained quantization.

comparisons/naive-vs-advanced-vs-agentic.title: Naive RAG vs Advanced RAG vs Agentic RAG
comparisons/naive-vs-advanced-vs-agentic.summary: Three evolutionary phases of RAG: naive (fixed pipeline, 2020-2023), advanced (optimized retrieval + reranking, 2023-2025), and agentic (self-correcting agent loops, 2025+) with increasing complexity and quality.

comparisons/o3-vs-r1-vs-claude-reasoning.title: OpenAI o3 vs DeepSeek R1 vs Claude Extended Thinking
comparisons/o3-vs-r1-vs-claude-reasoning.summary: Head-to-head comparison of the three leading reasoning model approaches: o3 (dense transformer, hidden CoT, MCTS), R1 (MoE, visible CoT, GRPO), and Claude 3.7 (hybrid toggle, visible thinking, logarithmic budget scaling).

comparisons/obsidian-vs-graph-database.title: Obsidian (File-Based) vs. Graph Database Storage
comparisons/obsidian-vs-graph-database.summary: Comparing file-system-based knowledge storage (markdown + Obsidian) with graph database storage (SQLite, Neo4j) as substrates for LLM-maintained knowledge bases.

comparisons/obsidian-vs-logseq-vs-notion.title: Obsidian vs Logseq vs Notion
comparisons/obsidian-vs-logseq-vs-notion.summary: 2026 comparison of the three dominant PKM tools: Obsidian (local-first markdown, best for Zettelkasten), Logseq (open-source outliner, best for structured organization), Notion (cloud-first, best for team collaboration) — with performance benchmarks and AI feature analysis.

comparisons/ocr-vs-vlm-document-processi.title: Traditional OCR vs Vision Language Models for Document Processing
comparisons/ocr-vs-vlm-document-processi.summary: Traditional OCR (Tesseract, Surya) excels at speed and clean text extraction; VLMs (Qwen2.5-VL, RolmOCR) understand context and layout; the hybrid OCR+VLM approach outperforms both — 2026 best practice.

comparisons/ollama-vs-vllm.title: Ollama vs vLLM
comparisons/ollama-vs-vllm.summary: Ollama: best for development and single-user (simple CLI, 41 TPS); vLLM: best for production and multi-user (PagedAttention, 793 TPS, linear scaling).

comparisons/open-source-vs-closed-llms.title: Open-Source vs Closed-Source LLMs
comparisons/open-source-vs-closed-llms.summary: Performance gap near zero by 2026; open-source ~10x cheaper per token but requires $125-190K/year infrastructure; 87% enterprise workloads still on closed but shifting to 50-50.

comparisons/pdf-parsers-comparison.title: PDF Parser Comparison: PyMuPDF vs Docling vs Unstructured vs Nougat vs LlamaParse
comparisons/pdf-parsers-comparison.summary: Head-to-head comparison of five PDF parsing tools across speed, accuracy, format support, deployment model, and use case fit — from PyMuPDF4LLM (fastest) to Nougat (best scientific) to Docling (best enterprise).

comparisons/personal-vs-enterprise-knowl.title: Personal vs. Team vs. Enterprise Knowledge Systems
comparisons/personal-vs-enterprise-knowl.summary: Three-tier comparison of knowledge systems from personal (1 user, ~100 articles, markdown + LLM) through team (5-50 users, wiki platforms) to enterprise (500-100K+ users, semantic layers + enterprise search + knowledge graphs). Each tier introduces qualitative new challenges: governance, federation, validation pipelines, and organizational change management.

comparisons/pinecone-vs-qdrant-vs-weavia.title: Pinecone vs Qdrant vs Weaviate
comparisons/pinecone-vs-qdrant-vs-weavia.summary: The three leading vector databases compared: Pinecone (managed simplicity + compliance), Qdrant (Rust performance + richest features), Weaviate (highest QPS + best hybrid search) — with detailed feature, performance, and pricing tables.

comparisons/ppo-vs-dpo.title: PPO vs DPO for LLM Alignment
comparisons/ppo-vs-dpo.summary: PPO consistently outperforms DPO on challenging tasks (code, complex reasoning) due to online learning and distribution robustness, but DPO's simplicity, lower compute, and accessibility make it the default for resource-constrained settings.

comparisons/process-vs-outcome-supervisi.title: Process Supervision vs Outcome Supervision
comparisons/process-vs-outcome-supervisi.summary: Comparison of two approaches to training reasoning verifiers: process supervision (step-level feedback, 78% on MATH, better alignment) vs. outcome supervision (answer-only feedback, cheaper to label but weaker performance and less interpretable).

comparisons/rag-vs-cag.title: RAG vs Cache-Augmented Generation (CAG)
comparisons/rag-vs-cag.summary: CAG preloads all documents into KV cache for 10x faster, more accurate inference on small KBs — but RAG remains necessary for large, dynamic corpora that exceed context window limits.

comparisons/rag-vs-fine-tuning.title: RAG vs. Fine-Tuning
comparisons/rag-vs-fine-tuning.summary: RAG injects knowledge at inference time (dynamic, traceable, per-query cost); fine-tuning bakes knowledge into weights (persistent, fast, upfront cost) — hybrid approaches like RAFT combine both.

comparisons/rag-vs-index-based-retrieval.title: RAG vs. Index-Based Retrieval
comparisons/rag-vs-index-based-retrieval.summary: Comparing vector-database RAG pipelines with Karpathy's index-based LLM navigation for knowledge base Q&A -- when each approach is appropriate and why.

comparisons/rag-vs-long-context.title: RAG vs Long Context Windows
comparisons/rag-vs-long-context.summary: RAG wins on cost (10x cheaper), latency (30-60x faster), and precision; long context wins on full-document reasoning and simplicity; hybrid approaches combining both are the pragmatic standard.

comparisons/ragas-vs-deepeval.title: RAGAS vs DeepEval
comparisons/ragas-vs-deepeval.summary: RAGAS is the RAG-specialized evaluation framework with reference-free metrics and synthetic data generation; DeepEval is the broader LLM evaluation framework with 14+ metrics, Pytest-like API, and CI/CD integration.

comparisons/rdf-vs-property-graph.title: RDF vs Property Graph
comparisons/rdf-vs-property-graph.summary: RDF (edge-centric, W3C-standardized, reasoning-capable) vs property graphs (node-centric, performance-optimized, developer-friendly) — two fundamentally different approaches to implementing knowledge graphs.

comparisons/react-vs-reflection-vs-plann.title: ReAct vs Reflection vs Planning
comparisons/react-vs-reflection-vs-plann.summary: Three complementary agent reasoning patterns: ReAct (interleaved reasoning-action loops), Reflection (self-critique and iterative improvement), and Planning (upfront task decomposition).

comparisons/rlhf-alternatives.title: RLHF Alternatives: DPO vs KTO vs IPO vs ORPO vs SPIN
comparisons/rlhf-alternatives.summary: Systematic comparison of 9+ preference alignment methods across data requirements, compute costs, pipeline complexity, and performance -- no single method wins everywhere; data quality and use case determine the best choice.

comparisons/rlhf-vs-constitutional-ai.title: RLHF vs Constitutional AI
comparisons/rlhf-vs-constitutional-ai.summary: Comparison of RLHF (human preference labels) and Constitutional AI (principle-guided self-critique): trade-offs in scalability, consistency, transparency, and alignment robustness.

comparisons/schema-guided-vs-schema-free.title: Schema-Guided vs. Schema-Free Extraction
comparisons/schema-guided-vs-schema-free.summary: Schema-guided extraction (OntoGPT, KARMA) trades flexibility for precision; schema-free extraction (KGGen, OpenIE) discovers novel patterns but requires post-processing — hybrid approaches are converging.

comparisons/self-attention-vs-cross-atte.title: Self-Attention vs Cross-Attention
comparisons/self-attention-vs-cross-atte.summary: Self-attention captures within-sequence relationships (Q, K, V from same source) while cross-attention connects two sequences (Q from decoder, K/V from encoder) — self-attention dominates decoder-only LLMs, cross-attention remains essential for multimodal, retrieval-augmented, and encoder-decoder tasks.

comparisons/semantic-vs-keyword-search.title: Semantic Search vs Keyword Search
comparisons/semantic-vs-keyword-search.summary: Complementary retrieval approaches: semantic search captures meaning via dense vectors but misses exact identifiers; keyword search matches precise terms via inverted indexes but misses synonyms — production systems combine both.

comparisons/single-agent-vs-multi-agent.title: Single-Agent vs. Multi-Agent Knowledge Pipelines
comparisons/single-agent-vs-multi-agent.summary: Comparing Karpathy's single-LLM approach (one model per phase) with multi-agent architectures (KARMA's 9 agents, STORM's perspective agents) for knowledge extraction and synthesis.

comparisons/softmax-vs-linear-attention.title: Softmax Attention vs Linear Attention
comparisons/softmax-vs-linear-attention.summary: Softmax attention (O(N^2*d), exact, sharp retrieval) vs linear attention (O(N*d^2), approximate, blurred retrieval): linear attention offers theoretical efficiency but consistently underperforms due to lost injectivity and sharpness — hybrid approaches or FlashAttention often preferred.

comparisons/static-vs-dynamic-benchmarks.title: Static vs Dynamic LLM Benchmarks
comparisons/static-vs-dynamic-benchmarks.summary: Static benchmarks (MMLU, HumanEval) enable precise comparison but suffer from contamination and saturation; dynamic benchmarks (Chatbot Arena, LiveCodeBench) resist gaming but make historical comparison harder.

comparisons/storm-vs-karpathy-workflow.title: STORM vs. Karpathy Workflow
comparisons/storm-vs-karpathy-workflow.summary: Comparing STORM's single-shot automated article generation from web search with Karpathy's persistent, accumulating knowledge base that grows through iterative compilation and the filing loop.

comparisons/symbolic-vs-neural-knowledge.title: Symbolic vs. Neural Knowledge Representation
comparisons/symbolic-vs-neural-knowledge.summary: Comparison of explicit symbolic KR (rules, ontologies, KGs) vs. implicit neural KR (LLM parametric knowledge) — each with complementary strengths, motivating hybrid architectures.

comparisons/text-rag-vs-multimodal-rag.title: Text RAG vs Multimodal RAG
comparisons/text-rag-vs-multimodal-rag.summary: Text-only RAG is simpler and sufficient for pure-text KBs; multimodal RAG adds image/chart retrieval via CLIP-style embeddings or text grounding — needed when visual content carries essential information.

comparisons/transformers-vs-state-space-.title: Transformers vs State Space Models
comparisons/transformers-vs-state-space-.summary: Transformers excel on semantically tokenized text with exact recall; SSMs dominate on raw/byte-level data with linear complexity — hybrid architectures (3:1 to 10:1 SSM:attention) emerging as optimal.

comparisons/unstructured-vs-langchain.title: Unstructured vs LangChain for Document Processing
comparisons/unstructured-vs-langchain.summary: Unstructured specializes in document ETL (parsing, partitioning, chunking) while LangChain is an LLM orchestration framework — they complement rather than compete, with Unstructured for ingestion and LangChain for downstream processing.

comparisons/vector-db-vs-bm25-search.title: Vector Database vs. BM25 Keyword Search
comparisons/vector-db-vs-bm25-search.summary: Comparing dense vector semantic search with sparse keyword-based BM25 retrieval -- and why hybrid approaches combining both outperform either alone.

comparisons/vibe-coding-vs-agentic-engin.title: Vibe Coding vs Agentic Engineering
comparisons/vibe-coding-vs-agentic-engin.summary: Two approaches to AI-assisted programming -- both coined/popularized by Karpathy -- compared: vibe coding (accept AI output with minimal review) vs agentic engineering (orchestrate agents with engineering discipline), representing the maturation from hype to production.

comparisons/vllm-vs-sglang.title: vLLM vs SGLang
comparisons/vllm-vs-sglang.summary: vLLM is the safe production default (broadest hardware, mature ops); SGLang is the throughput leader for multi-turn/agentic workloads (29% faster, automatic KV cache reuse via RadixAttention).

comparisons/zettelkasten-vs-basb.title: Zettelkasten vs Building a Second Brain
comparisons/zettelkasten-vs-basb.summary: Two dominant PKM methodologies compared: Zettelkasten optimizes for thinking and insight generation through atomic, densely-linked notes; BASB optimizes for creative output through actionable organization (PARA) and progressive distillation (CODE).
